title: ESQL: Preserve the projection of an aggregation

timeline.message:
ESQL: Preserve the projection of an aggregation

The internal AggregateOperators are focused creating groups and
 performing the aggregations using their intermediate states. However
 the logical projection is not enforced leading to errors downstream.
 Currently this is handled through OutputOperator which forces an
 alignment between the layout and the attributes however this is not
 only fragile but also insufficient.

This commit fixes a couple of things:
- introduces a ProjectOperator in front of the AggregateOperator.
 This is much easier, at least at the moment as it keeps the agg logic
 untouched.
- improves the ProjectOperator by moving away from the BitSet to a List
 that handles not just the selection but also ordering

Fix #99782

timeline.body:
The internal AggregateOperators are focused creating groups and
 performing the aggregations using their intermediate states. However
 the logical projection is not enforced leading to errors downstream.
 Currently this is handled through OutputOperator which forces an
 alignment between the layout and the attributes however this is not
 only fragile but also insufficient.

This commit fixes a couple of things:
- introduces a ProjectOperator in front of the AggregateOperator. This is much easier, at least at the moment as it keeps the agg logic untouched.
- improves the ProjectOperator by moving away from the BitSet to a List that handles not just the selection but also ordering

Fix #99782
This looks like a leftover, is this intended to be part of this PR?

To confirm that this fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/99888, we could add a csv test with the offending query:
```
from employees | stats m1 = max(salary), m2 = min(salary), m3 = min(salary), m4 = max(salary)
```

nit: variable name is a bit confusing now.

```suggestion
        var projection = randomProjection(size);
```

nit: looks like a typo here.
```suggestion
     * Creates an operator that applies the given projection, encoded as an integer list where
```

nit: since the project operator does not use a bit mask anymore, we should probably update its description.
```suggestion
        return "ProjectOperator[projection = " + projection + ']';
```

nit: for easier debugging, the error message could include the size of the page and the attempted projection index:
```suggestion
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cannot project block with index [" + source + "] from a page with size [" + page.geBlockCount() + "]");
```
Instead of creating this set on every call to `process` (often), this could be created in the constructor already since it only depends on the projection.

super-duper nit: looks like a typo
```suggestion
        var projection = new ArrayList<Integer>(size);
```
Since this will be iterated over often, an int array might be better rather than a list of boxed Integers.

This generally LGTM and could be merged without much change if it unblocks us.

However, since the local execution planner now plans projections differently, it would be nice to have unit tests that make sure we cover all weird edge cases that could happen during planning; That includes the newly supported double projections and reorderings.

Other than that I have mostly minor remarks.
Other than what @alex-spies mentioned about the additional test covering https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/99888 fix, LGTM.
